source: hand-authored fixture for issue #309 — not shipped data
description: Shapes about whether a CONDITION rule's bare-containment match against a recorded condition is corroborated, for the injected record's patient-specific reading. The recorded condition names are taken from the OpenMRS 3.7.1 reference-application demo dictionary, the corpus issue #309's measurement was run over (the allergen 'Nefotenone' on the Nefopam entry is invented, and is not one of them). (1) Naltrexone rules on the condition token 'liver', which is the most plausible hepatic contraindication token there is and which nests inside every deliver/delivery form the dictionary publishes — 20 of the 30 values it matches over that dictionary's 2581 condition candidates, e.g. 'Status Post Cesarean Delivery'. (2) Acamprosate files the same TYPE and TOKEN as Naltrexone with the token padded ('  liver  '), under a note of its own so the two clauses stay distinguishable, because the witness filter trims a token and the boundary question must be put to the same string it trimmed — untrimmed, an operator's stray whitespace silently loses the recorded attribution. (3) Metformin rules on 'renal', which nests inside 'Malignant tumor of adrenal gland' — a tumour of a different organ. (4) Nefopam carries NO condition rule and is here for a coverage reason rather than a matching one: it re-pins the `continue` guard in DrugSafetyValidator.addContraindications, whose only previous witness used an unmatched CONDITION rule and which #309's change therefore disarmed — a self-named allergy rule 'nefo' that an allergen recorded as 'Nefotenone' reaches only mid-word, beside a CLASS allergy rule 'nsaid' that the same allergen does not match at all, both carrying ONE note, so the two keys render one clause string in the patient-specific SECTIONS (which dedupe by text); the record's full 'Contraindicated with:' list is keyed per rule and still prints that note twice, which is operator-authored-only and pre-existing. An unmatched non-self-named allergy rule still corroborates TRUE unconditionally, which is what makes it a witness the condition leg cannot silence. (5) Paracetamol rules on 'edema', whose mid-word matches are clinically RIGHT compounds ('Lymphedema', 'Angioedema') — the residue the boundary rule gives up, kept here so a future change can read what it costs. NO entry here files a 'peptic ulcer' condition rule, deliberately: the cases about that token are about the SHIPPED seed and go through DrugReferenceTestSupport.curatedService(), so a lookalike rule in this file would let a later case assert against the fixture while reading as though it asserted against the shipped data. No entry carries ATC codes or interactions, so no class comparison can chip and every record is the contraindication arms' own.
